newsitem.title: INDIA: India keen to export latex as local demand falls.
newsitem.headline: India keen to export latex as local demand falls.

text.p: Indian rubber traders are keen to explore avenues to export latex to world markets due to low domestic demand and relatively high global prices, state and industry officials said on Thursday.
They said falling domestic demand had dragged Indian rubber prices to levels lower than world prices.

"There is a crisis in the latex sector due to a drastic fall in consumption in the foam industry," state-run Rubber Board chairman K.J. Mathew told Reuters. "Therefore latex producers will have to reduce production and export some stocks."

Traders said the price of centrifugal latex had fallen to about 36 rupees a kg in the domestic markets from 70 rupees last year. Domestic prices were about four rupees lower than average world prices.
"This means that the producers can gain four rupees per kg if they export than depend on the domestic foam industry," said Thomas John, a dealer in the southern town of Coonoor.
Traders said some 15,000 to 20,000 tonnes of latex were stored at various processing centres in the country.
Demand for latex was low as foam bed and pillow manufacturers preferred imported polyurethane as it gave them a 10 percent cost advantage.
But board officials object to the use of polyurethane as it is inflammable, traders said.
Mathew said the board was keen to provide financial help to those who would export latex.
John said the export of latex was necessary to keep prices stable, but there were some inherent difficulties.
"Low quality of Indian latex, inadequate initiatives from the government and the need to impress as a regular supplier are the main factors," John said.

Traders said that to gain access to world markets, India needed to improve its latex quality by changing processing facilities and producing double centrifugal latex instead of the present single centrifugal latex.
"India is known all over the world as a net importer of rubber," John said. "So it takes time to gain acceptance as an exporter of latex."
Political leaders in the southern state of Kerala, which produces 95 percent of the country's rubber, have urged the government to export about 25,000 tonnes of rubber latex with immediate effect.
"The delay in deciding this has caused huge losses to the growers," said one leader.
The Rubber Board has estimated 1997/98 (April-March) natural rubber output at 579,000 tonnes against 549,000 tones in 1996/97.
